requirement:
The Rust outline profile under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` MUST
identify items by segments describing their syntactic ancestry within the file,
such as `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]`, and `mod[local]/fn[run]`, and MUST NOT
resolve Rust modules across files. Functions, methods, structs, enums, unions,
traits, impls, modules, macros, constants, statics, type aliases, and extern
blocks MUST be outline nodes. Impl segments MUST be named by their syntactic self
type and optional trait path, as `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`. `use`
declarations and other items without a suitable name MUST be anonymous. Selector
spelling MUST be documented.
rationale:
I found no gaps. Each obligation maps to marked code and to a test that asserts its outcome.

**Obligations and code**
- **Selector segments from syntactic ancestry.**
  - Rust has one outline node kind per mapped grammar kind, so selectors like `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]` and `mod[local]/fn[run]` come from nesting within one file.
  - This is `KINDS` and `PROFILE` in `src/outline/rust.rs` (lines 131–172), both marked `{impl}`.
  - `fn[outer]/fn[inner]` and `mod[local]/fn[run]` appear in the tests.
- **Modules not resolved across files.**
  - `mod_item` is named only by its `name` field. `mod external;` becomes `mod[external]` and nothing opens another file.
  - `rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry` asserts `mod[external]`.
- **Required node kinds.**
  - `KINDS` maps `function_item` and `function_signature_item` to `fn`, which covers functions, methods and trait method signatures.
  - It also maps `struct_item`, `enum_item`, `union_item`, `trait_item`, `impl_item`, `mod_item`, `macro_definition`, `const_item`, `static_item`, `type_item` and `foreign_mod_item`.
  - `rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry` asserts a selector for each of these.
- **Impl naming.**
  - `impl_name` (line 8) uses the `type` field plus the optional `trait` field.
  - The tests assert `impl[Thing]`, `impl[Thing/Trait]`, `impl[%5Bu8;%204%5D]` and `impl[Wrapper<T>/Trait]`.
- **Anonymous nodes.**
  - `use_declaration` and item-position `macro_invocation` use `NameRule::Anonymous`.
  - `item_macro` and `in_item_list` restrict macro invocations to item position.
  - Tests: `selectors_name_syntactic_ancestry_and_duplicates` asserts `use@` selectors that differ from each other. `item_macros_are_anonymous_nodes_and_expression_macros_are_not` asserts `macro@<12 hex>` selectors for item macros, and that expression macros inside function bodies are not nodes.
- **Extern blocks.**
  - `extern_name` (line 23) uses the ABI string, or `Rust` when none is written.
  - The tests assert `extern[C]` and `extern[Rust]`.
- **Selector spelling documented.**
  - `md/reference.md`, "Rust items" (line 592), gives examples and the impl naming rule. It also covers anonymous `use` and macro nodes, and says modules are never resolved across files.
  - The "Selectors" section and the "Outline profiles" table document the full spelling.

**Marking and unspecified behavior**
- The `{impl}` and `{test}` references on the sources above cover this code. I found no other implementing code that lacks a reference.
- `extern-crate` and `associated_type` nodes are extra outline kinds beyond the list. They come from named grammar nodes, and the profile table documents them. The text does not forbid them, so I count them as within what it describes.

**Testing**
- `rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry` covers every required kind, duplicate-name `#N` disambiguation, the no-ABI extern, and resolving each selector back to its node.
- `selectors_name_syntactic_ancestry_and_duplicates` covers anonymous `use`, impls, and nesting.
- `item_macros_are_anonymous_nodes_and_expression_macros_are_not` covers the macro cases.

text: :::{req} rust_item_selectors
The Rust outline profile under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` MUST
identify items by segments describing their syntactic ancestry within the file,
such as `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]`, and `mod[local]/fn[run]`, and MUST NOT
resolve Rust modules across files. Functions, methods, structs, enums, unions,
traits, impls, modules, macros, constants, statics, type aliases, and extern
blocks MUST be outline nodes. Impl segments MUST be named by their syntactic self
type and optional trait path, as `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`. `use`
declarations and other items without a suitable name MUST be anonymous. Selector
spelling MUST be documented.
:::{req} outlines
Habeas MUST parse Rust, Python, TypeScript, CSS, Markdown, TOML, and YAML
sources with pinned tree-sitter grammars, selected by file extension compared
case-insensitively. A source with any syntax error MUST fail to parse, reporting
the line of its first error. Every
other text file MUST use a plain-text profile in which each line that is not
blank is an anonymous outline node of kind `line`. Each supported language MUST
have an outline profile that maps grammar node kinds to short outline kind names
and, for each mapped kind, states whether a node is named, and by which fields
or children, or anonymous. Only mapped kinds MUST appear in the outline; other
nodes MUST be transparent, so their outline descendants appear under the
nearest outline ancestor. A profile MAY attach grammar siblings to an outline
node, such as Rust attributes and doc comments preceding an item, so the outline
tree need not match the grammar tree exactly; attached siblings are part of that
node for its line range and hash. Every file's outline MUST have a root node
for the whole file, independent of language. Source in no other outline node,
such as top-level statements no profile maps, MUST belong to the root node;
profiles MUST NOT invent fallback kinds for it. Comments MUST NOT be outline nodes. Profiles MUST be
documented. Upgrading a grammar or profile MAY change outlines and MUST be
treated as a deliberate change.
:::{definition} definition_selection
:phrase: definition selection
A full requirement or example name, or a definition glob, identifying the
requirements and named examples it matches under
{cite}`requirements.references.definition_globs`. A name without `*` selects
exactly that definition.
